packagings.name: Factory Set
packagings.notes: Sold by Topps as the Complete Set: a sealed box holding the whole 700-card base set from both series, together with the short-print variations of #697-700, which are sold no other way. Its base cards are identical to the ones found in Series 1 and Series 2 packs. Documented by its own Topps checklist, the third source in provenance.

provenance.covers: the factory set: base #1-700 and the four short-print rookies
provenance.notes: Independent confirmation of the whole base set: all 700 card numbers, names and teams agree with the two series checklists, as do the four short-print rookies. The sources disagree only on ten designations — this one prints "Combo Card" (CC) where the series checklists print "Combo Card/Checklist" (CC CL) for #52, 118, 122, 126, 168, 197, 236, 260, 265, 302. The series checklists are followed here as the more specific of the two.

notes: One set issued in two waves; the factory set is a packaging of the whole 700-card base, not a separate set. Two variation programs are kept apart because Topps prints genuinely different names for them across series and merging would be a guess: Vintage Stock (Series 1) vs Vintage Stock Retro (Series 2),. Short Print Rookies reuse base numbers #697-700 — see schema/1.0/ROW-FORMAT.md, Numbering scope. Rookie 1952 (Series 1, #4-339) and 1952 (Series 2, #372-668) are one 45-card variation programme continuing across the two waves, not two: their numbers never collide, and TCDB counts the pair as a single 45-card sub-collection. Kept under the general printed name.
